thread:
maya: Heads up — saw a class of resume bugs after the fallback routing change. Clients resumed, resume was accepted, but SSE payloads were corrupted / duplicated for ~5% of sessions.

maya: Investigated logs: resume accepted on proxy in eu-west, but the backend shard id didn't match the resume's expected shard. KV cache replay ended up mixing sequence numbers.

maya: log snippet:
```
[2026-03-22T17:46:12Z] resume_token=abc123 tenant=acme route=eu-west proxy_shard=3 backend_shard=5 resume:accepted
[2026-03-22T17:46:12Z] kv_replay: seq_expected=120 seq_seen=33 -> payload_mismatch
[2026-03-22T17:46:12Z] emit: client_seen_duplicate_event id=evt_987
```

josh: hmm that screams namespace not encoded in the resume token. If two proxies map resume_token -> different shard namespace, they can accept a token intended for another route.

arun: We currently sign resume tokens with tenant+session_id+expiry only. We intentionally avoided route/replica metadata so tokens survive small route moves, but this breaks when fallback switches across pool topologies.

lina: Do we have metrics for resume_shard_mismatch? I can only see resume_accept / resume_reject counts in console, not mismatch. Console billing shows duplicate token consumption which customers are noticing.

farah: @lina yes, customer reported duplicated token counts in per-route dashboard. We need a way to flag these resumes as "shard-mismatch" and surface deduped billing in the UI.

josh: Proposed immediate mitigation: on resume, validate that `resume.token_shard_hash == backend.shard_hash`, else reject and force full reconnect. That will increase cold reconnects but avoids garbled payloads and double-counting.

maya: +1 for validation. Also suggest emitting a new metric `resume_shard_mismatch{route,region}` and a trace event `resume.reject:shard_mismatch` containing the token id (hashed) for debugging.

arun: Long term: include route_version and shard_id in the resume token signature so resume is only valid for compatible backends. Also add a graceful TTL where token can be replayed across minor topology moves if route_version matches.

lina: For console UX: add a toggle to show "deduped resume billing" and a queryable tag `shard_mismatch=true`. We can backfill 48h by matching duplicate event ids, but won't be perfect.

farah: Deployment plan? Canary FLAG on 10% of traffic, route-aware resume enabled. Need rollout doc and cost/latency dashboard snippet.

maya: Plan of record:
- short: reject shard-mismatched resumes server-side + emit metric (maya)
- mid: token includes route metadata + signed shard (arun)
- console: metric + deduped billing UI (lina/farah)
- rollout: feature flag + 10% canary then 100% in 2 weeks (josh/ops)

ops-bot: deploy/links canary-playbook -> https://deploy.internal/redwood/canary/1711206789

josh: I'll add the server-side check and the metric today. Maya can wire traces. Lina/farah, can you scope console changes?

lina: Yep, I'll put a small RFC in docs and start the UI PR.

arun: Will prototype token format and backward-compatible verification.

maya: Great. If we see customer-facing duplicates during the canary we can flip fallback routing to strict affinity until tokens roll out.

farah: I'll add a dashboard panel for `resume_shard_mismatch` and a customer alert rule.

maya: Thanks all. Keeping thread here for rollout updates and any odd log samples.
